name: La Belle Lucie
description: La Belle Lucie (also known as Lovely Lucy or Three Shuffles and a Draw) is a classic 'Fan' type solitaire game. It is known for its high difficulty and the requirement for careful planning. Unlike Klondike, all cards are dealt face-up into 17 three-card fans, allowing the player to see the entire deck from the start. However, only the top card of each fan is playable, making card blocking a constant challenge.

history.origins: Dates to the 19th-century French card salons. It is one of the earliest 'Perfect Information' solitaires, where no cards are hidden.
timeline: 1850s: First described in French patience manuals.
1870s: Becomes a popular parlor game in Victorian England.
1990s: Included as a standard 'Fan' game in many PC solitaire collections.
Present: Remains a staple for experienced solitaire enthusiasts seeking a challenge.
history.cultural: Named after a legendary French beauty, the game's fan structure mimics a folding hand fan.
history.evolution: The game's distinctive 'Mercy' rule (The Draw) was added later to make the game slightly more winnable.

setup.players: One player only. La Belle Lucie is a patience (solitaire) game played by a single player, who moves cards from the tableau fans to the four foundations. There are no partners or opponents.
setup.dealing: Deal all 52 cards face-up into 17 fans of three cards each and one single card as the 18th fan. When redealing, reshuffle and redeal in the same pattern (fans of three with remainder as last fan).
setup.equipment: Table space for 18 fan piles and four foundation piles.

rules.objective: Move all cards to the four foundation piles, building up in suit from Ace to King.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Foundations**: Build up by suit (A, 2, 3... K).
2. **Tableau**: Only the top card of a fan is playable to another fan or a foundation.
3. **Building**: On the tableau, build cards DOWN by suit (e.g., 9 of Hearts on 10 of Hearts). Moving sequences is NOT allowed.
4. **Empty Spaces**: Once a fan is cleared, that space cannot be refilled.
keyRules: Only the top card of each fan is playable.
Foundations build up by suit from Ace to King.
Tableau builds down by suit; moving sequences is not allowed.
Empty fan spaces cannot be refilled.
Two reshuffles and redeals allowed when stuck.

strategy.basic: Prioritize exposing Aces. If an Ace is trapped under two high cards (like a King and Queen), you will likely need to rely on the shuffles to free it.
strategy.intermediate: The King Trap: Avoid moving a card onto a King unless absolutely necessary. Since Kings are the highest cards, they can never be moved onto another card, meaning any card underneath a King in a fan is potentially permanently blocked.
strategy.advanced: Staged Progression: Don't move every possible card to the foundations immediately. Sometimes it is better to keep a card on the tableau to serve as a 'landing spot' for a lower card of the same suit.
tips: Use your shuffles strategically. Don't shuffle if you still have viable moves, as the redeal is entirely random and can worsen your position.
If you see three cards of the same suit in reverse order (e.g., 5-6-7), you are in luckâ€”these will reveal themselves sequentially as you play.
Save the 'Mercy' draw for an Ace or a 2 that is buried at the very bottom of a fan.
